observed_vs_expected: The observed best_target_score decreased from 0.8649257273997111 in Round 1 to 0.7605299445492656 in Round 2, a drop of approximately 0.1044. This directly contradicts the expected observation that the score should increase with period scaling optimization. The tightest_margin remained stable at 0.42368400158897357, consistent with the expectation that margin would not collapse, but the magnitude of the score regression indicates the current optimization trajectory did not yield improvements as hypothesized.
deviation_mechanism: Period scaling modifies the optical path length of each layer, shifting interference fringes. The current scaling constraint restricts the optimizer to a narrow window that forces layer thicknesses toward integer quarter-wave ratios. In Round 2, candidates cluster near these rigid ratios (e.g., High-index layers hover around 80-107 nm while Low-index layers sit near 20-35 nm). This periodic bias causes the 200-400 nm reflectance band and 800-1500 nm transmittance band to spectrally overlap more severely than in Round 1, increasing parasitic reflections in the passband and dropping the weighted objective. The restricted scaling search space prevents crossing the spectral crossover point where fringe decoupling restores higher scores.
